subject.title: Duplicate slug rows after squat removal break publish/scan pipeline — new versions never go live (shieldcortex stuck at 4.47.12)

question: Which `shieldcortex` record is the authoritative publisher-owned skill, and which deletion/redirect state may automated reconciliation treat as ineligible for slug resolution?
rationale: The correct result depends on content-rights and moderation history that source code cannot safely infer; choosing the wrong row could change publisher ownership or the security state shown to installers.

options.title: Reconcile with content-rights audit
options.body: Verify the authoritative row from the resolved claim, preserve its versions and moderation record, and terminalize or redirect only the confirmed noncanonical rows before hardening shared lookups.

options.title: Keep fail-closed pending manual cleanup
options.body: Leave duplicate-slug resolution failing until staff complete a production data reconciliation, avoiding any automatic selection of a canonical listing.

recommendation.title: Reconcile with content-rights audit
recommendation.body: Verify the authoritative row from the resolved claim, preserve its versions and moderation record, and terminalize or redirect only the confirmed noncanonical rows before hardening shared lookups.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns the adjacent publish-attempt recovery path and is the strongest available routing signal for coordinating the bounded follow-up.
